1.      Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,
please include the following: (1) identification of all parties, (2) description of the applicant and it’s
licensure track record, (3) the type of transaction proposed including description of the transaction and
relevant costs, (4) summary of all transfer documents, (5) summary of the organizational structure of the
applicant and its affiliates, and (6) whether the facility will be accredited (e.g. TJC, CHAP, etc.).

This application involves Hebert Health Center, a 133 bed skilled nursing facility located at 180 Log
Road, Smithfield, Rhode Island (the “Hebert Facility”) and is contemporaneously submitted with the
CEC application involving Trinity Health & Rehab Center (the “Trinity Facility”), a 185 bed skilled
nursing facility located at 4 Saint Joseph Street, Woonsocket, Rhode Island. Both the Hebert Facility
and Trinity Facility are the subject of the Providence Superior Court (the “Superior Court”)
receivership proceedings with the management and supervision under Jeremy B. Savage, Esquire,
solely in his role as Court Appointed Receiver (“Receiver”) for the Hebert Facility Operator and
Trinity Facility Operator, respectively, pursuant to an Order of the Superior Court dated June 21,
2023, PC2023-02885 (the “Receivership Action”). As part of the Receivership Action, on June 23,
2023, the Receiver entered into a Management Agreement with Allaire Healthcare, Inc., approved
by the Superior Court with an effective date of July 18, 2023. Yehuda “Jay” Yarmush, Allaire’s
Managing Partner has lead the management team for both the Hebert Facility and Trinity Facility.
During that time and under Mr. Yarmush’s leadership, the facilities have improved their quality of
care and expanded specialty services provided to its residents. In addition, under Mr. Yarmush’s
leadership, the census at both facilities has increased and the financial status of both facilities has
improved dramatically. This application seeks approval for the acquisition of the real estate and
operations of the Hebert Facility, pursuant to an agreement approved by the Superior Court,
Associate Justice Brian P. Stern on November 4, 2024.

The proposed transaction approved by the Superior Court involves (i) Cedar Haven Operations LLC
d/b/a Lake Forest Health & Rehabilitation LLC, , a Pennsylvania limited liability company (“Hebert
Opco” or “Applicant”), and (ii) Lake Forest Health & Rehabilitation Propco LLC, a Rhode Island
limited liability company (“Hebert Propco”) regarding the acquisition by Hebert Opco and Hebert
Propco of substantially all the assets and real estate related to the Hebert Facility from ASLC RI II,
LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (the “Current Hebert Operator”) and Summit
Smithfield, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “Current Hebert Property Owner”).

On November 4, 2024, the Superior Court, Associate Justice Brian P. Stern, entered an order in the
Receivership Action which provided, among other things, approval for the Receiver’s petition to sell
(i) all of the assets which comprise the Hebert Facility, including the real estate and all improvements,
pursuant to the terms of a proposed (a) Agreement for Purchase and Sale by and between Hebert
Propco and Current Hebert Property Owner (the ‘Hebert Purchase Agreement”) and (b) the Asset
Purchase Agreement. Copies of the agreements are at Tab 14.

The purchase price for the Hebert Facility real property and improvements pursuant to the Hebert
Purchase Agreement is Five Million Nine Hundred Forty-Seven Thousand Six Hundred Eighty and
91/100 Dollars ($5,947,680.91). The purchase price of substantially all the assets of both Current
Hebert Operator and the current Trinity Operator pursuant to the Asset Purchase Agreement is
Three Million Eight Hundred Twenty-Six Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty-Four Dollars and Fifty-
One Cents ($3,826,724.51) broken down as follows:

(i) Allaire Health Care, Inc.’s forgiveness of the Management Loan as defined in that certain Superior
Court approved Management Agreement, valued in the amount of One Million Five Hundred
Thousand Dollars ($1,500,000.00); and

(ii)  Payment of Two Million Three Hundred Twenty-Six Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty-Four
and 51/100 Dollars ($2,326,724.51) via wire transfer of immediately available funds.

The Applicant

The Applicant is wholly owned by Lake Valley Operations Holdco LLC, in turn owned 80% by Mr.
Yarmush and 20% by ESRI Holdco LLC. ESRI’s members include Ephraim Nussbaum and Shlomo
Heller, with 50%/50% ownership interests. Mr. Yarmush has extensive experience in nursing home
operations and prior to his employment with Allaire has had extensive experience with nursing home
operations in Ohio, Alabama, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee. Mr. Yarmush has a
proven track record of turning around underperforming facilities, transforming facilities that were
losing millions of dollars annually into proﬁtable enterprises.

Mr. Yarmush excels in building strong teams that are dedicated to providing high-quality care. He
prioritizes staﬀ development and engagement, fostering a culture of excellence and collaboration. His
initiatives have successfully reshaped the image of facilities within their communities, enhancing trust
and positive relationships with residents and their families.

A signiﬁcant focus of Mr. Yarmush’s work has been on eliminating reliance on staﬃng agencies,
resulting in improved care continuity and higher staﬀ retention rates. His strategic oversight has led
to strong census growth and signiﬁcant revenue enhancement, optimizing ﬁnancial performance
while maintaining high standards of service.

Skilled in managing care contracts, Mr. Yarmush has successfully negotiated favorable terms that
beneﬁt both the facilities and the communities they serve. He is experienced in navigating change in
ownership applications and works closely with legal ﬁrms on asset purchases and vendor
relationships to ensure compliance and operational eﬃciency.

Mr. Yarmush maintains constant contact with the facilities he oversees to monitor progress, address
challenges, and foster accountability. His hands-on approach ensures that every facility operates
smoothly and meets its ﬁnancial and care objectives. With a deep commitment to enhancing the
quality of life for residents and achieving operational success, Jay Yarmush is a leader in the nursing
home industry, dedicated to making a meaningful impact in every community he serves.
Please see Appendix B for a listing of facilities in which Mr. Nussbaum and Mr. Heller have
ownership interest in.

5.     Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and
operational policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care, services,
and accommodations, and a sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how the
proposal would advance these areas:

       a.      Resident’s physical environment:

                  i.   Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                       The Facility offers a number of options within the facility for resident
                       privacy needs, as well as for common areas with other residents and
                       staff members. All residents have either private or semi-private rooms.
                       The Facility also offers private spaces for residents to utilize during
                       family or other meetings.

                ii.    Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                       Whenever feasible and in the residents’ best interests, the Facility
                       honors patient requests and supports their autonomy.

                iii.   Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community
                       kitchen(s), laundry, activities;

                       The Facility offers a variety of amenities for residents to enjoy,
                       including an activity room, private hospice rooms, beauty
                       salon/barber, cable, wifi, country kitchen, dining room, complimentary
                       laundry facilities on site and housekeeping. Pets are permitted, there is
                       a pharmaceutical delivery service, and smoke free environment.

                iv.    Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens
                       and gardening);

                       Recognizing the importance of outdoor spaces to wellbeing of residents,
                       the Facility offers well maintained and quiet outdoor space for
                       residents to enjoy.

       b.      Resident-centered systems of care:

                  i.   Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice, and
                       negotiated risk;

                       While fostering autonomy, choice and negotiated risk, the Facility also
                       maintains adequate security systems to ensure each resident’s safety,



                                                     18

===== PAGE 21 =====
            such as a wander guard system. There are security systems in place to
            be resident-centered based on assessment by the clinical team.

      ii.   Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed,
            waking);

            Each resident’s daily routine is carefully planned for as determined by
            his or her initial and periodic assessments. Meals, activities, and care are
            offered based on each individual resident’s routine.

     iii.   Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

            The Facility offers a variety of food choices based on resident specific
            needs, ethnicity, culture, religious and resident preference. The Facility
            follows the minced and moist diet as recommended by the Academy of
            Nutritional and Dietetic Association.


      iv.   Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

            Residents have the opportunity to express their lifestyle choices during
            their individual assessment, as well as during their periodic assessments
            and care plan meetings, and any time in between.

c.   Workforce administration:

       i.   How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of
            resident services and foster relationship building?

            The Facility is staffed according to resident need. Employee assignments
            are also based on resident need and the timing of residents requiring
            specific services and care throughout the day. For direct care givers, the
            facility aims to maintain consistent staffing to specific resident locations.

      ii.   Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over (e.g.
            Registered nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

            The Facility is constantly recruiting licensed staff to deal with inevitable
            turn-over. Such recruiting occurs at nursing schools, through
            advertisements, and through informed referral networks and are
            monitored by the Personnel Director and Department heads. Flexible
            schedules are provided to meet staff and facility needs.

1.      Please provide an executive summary describing the nature and scope of the proposal. Additionally,

This Application involves Trinity Health & Rehab Center, a 185 bed skilled nursing facility located
at 4 Saint Joseph Street, Woonsocket, Rhode Island (the “Trinity Facility”) and is contemporaneously
submitted with the CEC application involving Hebert Health Center (the “Hebert Facility”), a 133
bed skilled nursing facility located at 180 Log Road, Smithfield, Rhode Island. Both the Trinity
Facility and the Hebert Facility are the subject of the Providence Superior Court (the “Superior
Court”) receivership proceedings with the management and supervision under Jeremy B. Savage,
Esquire, solely in his role as Court Appointed Receiver (“Receiver”) for the Trinity Facility Operator
and Hebert Facility Operator, respectively, pursuant to an Order of the Superior Court dated June
21, 2023, PC2023-02885 (the “Receivership Action”). As part of the Receivership Action, on June 23,
2023, the Receiver entered into a Management Agreement with Allaire Healthcare, Inc., approved
by the Superior Court with an effective date of July 18, 2023. Yehuda “Jay” Yarmush, Allaire’s
Managing Partner has lead the management team for both the Trinity Facility and Hebert Facility.
During that time and under Mr. Yarmush’s leadership, the facilities have improved their quality of
care and expanded specialty services provided to its residents. In addition, under Mr. Yarmush’s
leadership, the census at both facilities has increased and the financial status of both facilities has
improved dramatically. This application seeks approval for the acquisition of the real estate and
operations of the Trinity Facility, pursuant to an agreement approved by the Superior Court,
Associate Justice Brian P. Stern on November 4, 2024.

The proposed transaction approved by the Superior Court involves (i) Valley View Health &
Rehabilitation LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company f/k/a Cedar Haven Operations
Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Trinity Opco” or “Applicant”), and (ii) Valley
View Health & Rehabilitation Propco LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (“Trinity
Propco”) regarding the acquisition by Trinity Opco and Trinity Propco of substantially all the assets
and real estate related to the Trinity Facility from ASLC OPCO RI I, LLC, a Rhode Island limited
liability company (the “Current Trinity Operator”) and Summit Woonsocket, LLC, a Delaware
limited liability company (the “Current Trinity Property Owner”).

On November 4, 2024, the Superior Court, Associate Justice Brian P. Stern, entered an order in the
Receivership Action which provided, among other things, approval for the Receiver’s petition to sell
(i) all of the assets which comprise the Trinity Facility, including the real estate and all improvements,
pursuant to the terms of a proposed (a) Agreement for Purchase and Sale by and between Trinity
Propco and Current Trinity Property Owner (the ‘Trinity Purchase Agreement”) and (b) Asset
Purchase Agreement. Copies of the agreements are at Tab 14.

5.     Based on the format below, please provide a summary of the applicant’s administrative and
operational policies and procedures to provide individualized and resident-centered care,
services, and accommodations, and a sense of peace, safety, and community, and clearly identify how
the proposal would advance these areas:

       a.     Resident’s physical environment:

                 i.   Accommodations for privacy vs. congregate and common areas;

                      The Facility offers a number of options within the facility for resident
                      privacy needs, as well as for common areas with other residents and
                      staff members. All residents have either private or semi-private
                      rooms. The Facility also offers private spaces for residents to utilize
                      during family or other meetings.

                ii.   Choice and autonomy in personal space, fixtures, furniture;

                      Whenever feasible and in the residents’ best interests, the Facility
                      honors patient requests and supports their autonomy.

               iii.   Access to and involvement in decentralized services, such as, community
                      kitchen(s), laundry, activities;

                      The Facility offers a variety of amenities for residents to enjoy,
                      including an activity room, private hospice rooms, beauty
                      salon/barber, cable, wifi, country kitchen, dining room,
                      complimentary laundry facilities on site and housekeeping. Pets are
                      permitted, there is a pharmaceutical delivery service, and smoke free
                      environment.

               iv.    Access to outdoors and outdoor activities (e.g., sunrooms, patios, gardens
                      and gardening);

                      Recognizing the importance of outdoor spaces to wellbeing of
                      residents, the Facility offers well maintained and quiet outdoor space
                      for residents to enjoy.

       b.     Resident-centered systems of care:

                 i.   Security systems and care delivery systems to foster autonomy, choice,
                      and negotiated risk;

                      While fostering autonomy, choice and negotiated risk, the Facility
                      also maintains adequate security systems to ensure each resident’s


                                                   18

===== PAGE 48 =====
            safety, such as a wander guard system and pass codes for each floor.
            There are security systems in place to be resident-centered based on
            assessment by the clinical team.

      ii.   Individualized daily/nightly scheduling (e.g., daily rhythm, going to bed,
            waking);

            Each resident’s daily routine is carefully planned for as determined
            by his or her initial and periodic assessments. Meals, activities, and
            care are offered based on each individual resident’s routine.

     iii.   Dining flexibility (e.g., time, access to dining style and menu choice);

            The Facility offers a variety of food choices based on resident specific
            needs, ethnicity, culture, religious and resident preference.


      iv.   Lifestyle/activities flexibility;

            Residents have the opportunity to express their lifestyle choices
            during their individual assessment, as well as during their periodic
            assessments and care plan meetings, and any time in between.

c.   Workforce administration:

       i.   How do staffing schedules and assignments ensure consistent delivery of
            resident services and foster relationship building?

            The Facility is staffed according to resident need. Employee
            assignments are also based on resident need and the timing of
            residents requiring specific services and care throughout the day. For
            direct care givers, the facility aims to maintain consistent staffing to
            specific resident locations.

      ii.   Administrative status strategies for dealing with licensed staff turn-over
            (e.g. Registered nurses, Licenses Practical nurses, Nursing Assistants)

            The Facility is constantly recruiting licensed staff to deal with
            inevitable turn-over. Such recruiting occurs at nursing schools,
            through advertisements, and through informed referral networks.

                                CONSULTING AGREEMENT

       THIS CONSULTING AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is entered into and effective as
of ______________ __, 2025 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Cedar Haven Operations
LLC, a Pennsylvania limited liability company (referred to herein as “Company”), and Lake
Valley RI Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Consultant”).

        IN CONSIDERATION of the mutual covenants, promises and conditions contained
herein, the parties agree as follows:

Section 1.     Consulting Services.

        A.       Consultant will provide the initial, and the ongoing, consulting services as
described on Exhibit “A” hereto, and such other duties as agreed by Company and Consultant
(collectively, the “Services”), to that certain long term care facility located at 180 Log Rd.
Smithfield, RI 02917 (“Facility”). Consultant shall adhere to Company and Facility policies,
practices and controls, and utilize Company and Facility systems.

Section 2.     Term/Termination.

        A.      This Agreement shall commence as of the Effective Date and shall thereafter
continue for one (1) year, and shall be renewable for five (5) successive additional terms of one
(1) year each upon the parties’ mutual consent. Thereafter, this Agreement shall renew annually
for a one (1) year term until one party gives the other written notice of its intent not to renew at
least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the existing term (the “Term”).

       B.      Either party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any or
no reason, upon ninety (90) days prior written notice to the other party. Further, this Agreement
may be terminated immediately by Company upon written notice to Consultant in the event of
Consultant’s gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud in the performance of obligations under
this Agreement.

       C.     In the event of termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 2(B) or
otherwise, Consultant shall reasonably cooperate in good faith to transition the provision of
Services to Company or its designees as expeditiously as is then reasonably practicable.
Section 3.     Compensation. In consideration of the performance of the Services, Company
shall pay Consultant a consulting fee (“Monthly Fee”) equal to five percent (5%) of the revenues
received from all sources in connection with the Facility during such period of time; provided that
the revenue shall not include or mean (i) interest or investment income of Company, (ii) capital
contributions to Company, (iii) insurance proceeds (provided however, business interruption
insurance proceeds shall be included in revenue), (iv) tax refunds, condemnation proceeds or
awards, and (v) amounts collected as trust funds or security deposits, if any, except to the extent
those security deposits are actually applied against the payments owed to the Facility.

Section 4.    Independent Contractor Status. Consultant shall not be deemed a Company
employee for the purpose of this Agreement and, on the contrary, shall be considered and treated
as an independent contractor for such purposes. Consultant specifically acknowledges and affirms

===== PAGE 59 =====
that Consultant is an independent contractor and understands the duties and responsibilities (and
the corresponding diminution in Company’s duties and responsibilities) resulting from such status.
Consultant shall be exclusively responsible for the payment of all taxes, withholding payments,
penalties, interest, fringe benefits, contributions to insurance and pension or other deferred
compensation plans including, without limitation, Workers’ Compensation and Social Security,
wages of any personnel under the employ of Consultant, and the filing of all necessary documents,
forms and returns pertinent to all of the foregoing.

Section 5.     Authority. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Consultant
may not bind Company in any way, whether orally or in writing, and Consultant may not lead any
person or entity to believe the contrary. The parties acknowledge and agree that Consultant is not
and shall not be deemed to be an employee, partner, joint-venturer or agent of or with Company
by reason of this Agreement. Consultant will be solely an independent contractor of Company.

Section 6.      Representations and Warranties. Each party represents and warrants to the other
party that this Agreement will not cause or require such party to breach any obligation to, or
agreement or confidence with, any other person.

Section 7.      Confidentiality. Consultant hereby acknowledges that Company has made (or may
make) available to Consultant certain confidential and/or proprietary information of Company or
licensed to Company, including, without limitation, trade secrets (collectively, the “Confidential
Material”), and further acknowledges that Consultant has no rights in or to the Confidential
Material. Except for compliance with applicable law or a governmental request, Consultant shall
not make any disclosure of this Agreement, the terms of this Agreement, or any of the Confidential
Material. Except for compliance with applicable law or a governmental request, Consultant shall
not make any duplication or other copy of any of the Confidential Material. Upon Company’s
request, Consultant shall, in its discretion, either immediately return or destroy all Confidential
Material to Company. If Confidential Material is destroyed, as opposed to being returned, then
Consultant shall represent in writing to Company that such destruction was completed. Consultant
shall notify each person to whom any disclosure is made that such disclosure is made in
confidence, that the Confidential Material shall be kept in confidence by such person, and that
such person shall be bound by the provisions of this Section 7. All of Company’s books, records
and accounts, whether prepared by Consultant or otherwise coming into the possession of
Consultant, shall remain the exclusive property of Company. Upon the termination of this
Agreement, Consultant shall immediately deliver to the possession of Company all such books
and records. Notwithstanding the foregoing, “Confidential Material” does not include confidential
and proprietary information that (i) is or becomes generally available to the public, other than as a
result of disclosure by Consultant or its representatives in breach of this Agreement or (ii) is or
becomes available to Consultant on a non-confidential basis from a source other than Company or
someone bound to keep such information confidential.

Section 8.     Intellectual Property - Ownership of Materials Created by Consultant. All
work, materials, products, and modifications thereof, created at the request of Company, or
developed or prepared for Company by Consultant under this Agreement, including any program
images and viewable text, is the sole property of Company, and all right, title and interest therein
shall vest in Company and shall be deemed to be a “work made for hire” made in the course of
Services rendered hereunder. To the extent that title to any such works may not, by operation of

                                       Consulting Services

Consultant shall do the following with respect to the Facility:

   1. Resident Relations. Consult with Company in the operations of the Facility in compliance
      with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and administer a resident relations
      program which maintains visibility of consultant presence.

   2. Personnel. Advise Company with respect to employment decisions affecting on-site
      Facility employees. Except as provided herein, all on-site Facility employees shall at all
      times be Company’s employees and not employees of Consultant.

   3. Service Contracts. Recommend that Company enter into and renew contracts for
      electricity, gas, water, telephone, cable television, cleaning, fuel oil, elevator maintenance,
      vermin extermination, trash removal, linen service, pharmaceuticals and medical supplies,
      pharmacy consulting, medical director, physical and speech therapy, hospice services,
      medical equipment, and other services in the ordinary course of the operation of the
      Facility; recommend to Company the purchase of any supplies and equipment necessary
      to maintain and so operate the Facility; and ensure that Company receives any applicable
      discounts, rebates, or commissions obtained for purchases or otherwise.

   4. Maintenance and Repair. Recommend to Company any required maintenance for the
      Improvements and grounds of the Facility including, without limitation, interior and
      exterior cleaning, painting and decorating, plumbing, carpentry, and other normal
      maintenance and repair work.

   5. Collection. Recommend to Company best practices to request, demand, collect, receive,
      and receipt all charges due from residents and otherwise due Company with respect to the
      Facility. Consultant may recommend that certain uncollectible accounts be charged off to
      a bad debt expense after reasonable efforts have been exhausted for collections, subject to
      Company’s final approval.

   6. Expenses. Assist Company, as directed by Company, with the contest and/or payment of
      all Facility expenses on or before that date after which interest or penalty will begin to
      accrue thereon.

   7. Reports. As soon as reasonable and practicable each calendar month, render to Company a
      statement of income and expenses showing the results of operation of the Facility for the
      preceding month and of the fiscal year to date. As soon as reasonably practical, but in no
      event later than twenty (20) days following the close of each quarter, render to Company a
      statement of income and expenses showing the results of operation of the Facility for the
      preceding quarter and of the fiscal year to date. As soon as reasonable and practicable
      after the end of each fiscal year, Consultant shall deliver to Company profit and loss
      statements, prepared on an accrual basis in accordance with generally accepted accounting
      principles consistently applied. All such monthly reports shall be in the format normally
      utilized by Consultant. Company may, regularly and/or from time to time, require that the

===== PAGE 65 =====
         annual financial statements of the Facility be audited, reviewed or compiled by a reputable
         accounting firm. Additionally, Consultant shall provide Company with all such financial
         and other reports and/or documents as required by any lenders of Company to enable
         Company to comply with the reporting requirements set forth in the applicable loan
         documents.

    8. Records. Recommend and assist Company in implementing best practices for maintaining
       a system of office records, books, and accounts, and any additional information or records
       reasonably required by Company for the preparation of federal, state, and local tax returns,
       all in a manner reasonably satisfactory to Company. Company and others designated by
       Company, including Company’s auditors and accountants, shall have, upon reasonable
       notice to Consultant, during normal business hours, access to and the right to audit and
       make copies of such records, accounts, and books, and all vouchers, files and all other
       material pertaining to the Facility and this Agreement that may be maintained at the address
       of Consultant.

    9. Legal Proceedings. Consultant shall make recommendations to Company related to the
       institution and prosecution of such actions and proceedings necessary to effect the
       purposes, perform the services, and take the actions contemplated by this Agreement.

    10. Process Insurance Claims. If requested by Company, Consultant shall assist Company in
        the processing of all claims under any insurance coverages pertaining to the Facility in a
        reasonably expeditious manner, so as to minimize delay in receipt by the Facility of the
        proceeds of such insurance.

    11. Maintenance of Licenses. Assist Company in obtaining and maintaining all licenses and
        certifications required for operation of the Facility, such as contracts with fiscal
        intermediaries and agencies and eligibility for participation in any applicable third party
        payor or other medical reimbursement programs. All licenses and permits shall be obtained
        in the name and at the expense of Company unless otherwise stipulated pursuant to
        applicable regulation or unless otherwise agreed in writing between Company and
        Consultant. Further, Company shall remain directly responsible to all federal, state and
        local enforcing agencies for compliance with such provisions and maintain state and
        federal licensing and certification requirements from and after the effective date hereof.
        Consultant shall monitor and furnish copies of all surveys and notices of noncompliance to
        Company promptly upon receipt by Consultant.

    12. Rate Schedules. Assist in developing price and rate schedules satisfactory to Company;
        assist Company in obtaining approval of appropriate price schedules by government
        agencies and appropriate rate/reimbursement schedules from third-party paying agencies,
        if applicable; provide all statistical, financial, and other data necessary to obtain payment
        from the appropriate agencies, if applicable; and assist in effecting final settlement of
        claims for payment.

    13. Accounting and Report Supervision. Advise Company on best practices for, and assist
        Company in overseeing, the maintenance of all resident records required for the orderly
        billing for nursing and miscellaneous goods and/or services, and Consultant shall assist

    14. Cost Reports and Tax Returns. Any reports that may be required to be made under the
        Medicare or Medicaid Program (or any successor program) of the federal Department of

        assist with such contest as requested by Company.

        structures which take into account the financial obligations of the Facility and the level of
        rates at other comparable facilities in the market area.

                                            Exhibit B

                               BUSINESS ASSOCIATE ADDENDUM

This Business Associate Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of the Effective
Date of the CONSULTING AGREEMENT (“Consulting Agreement”) to which this Agreement
is attached by and between Company (“Covered Entity”) and Consultant (“Business Associate”),
and is attached to and made part of the Consulting Agreement. Covered Entity and Business
Associate are sometimes referred to individually as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”
Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings set forth in the Consulting
Agreement.

                                          RECITALS

     A. The Parties acknowledge that they are required to comply with the Health Insurance
        Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and its accompanying regulations as amended
        from time to time, including the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Heath
        Information (“Privacy Rule”) and the Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic
        Protected Health Information (the “Security Rule”), as well as Subtitle D of the Health
        Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (“HITECH”) of
        the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act and its accompanying regulations, as
        amended from time to time (collectively, “HIPAA”).

     B. Covered Entity is a “covered entity,” as defined in HIPAA.

     C. Business Associate is a “business associate” as defined by HIPAA.

D.      Business Associate provides consulting services to Covered Entity (collectively, the
        “Services”) in accordance with the Consulting Agreement to which this Agreement is
        attached. In accordance with the terms of the Consulting Agreement, Business Associate
        may use, disclose, create, receive, maintain, or transmit, as applicable, on behalf of
        Covered Entity, protected health information (“PHI”) for purposes of providing the
        Services.
E.      The Parties desire to conduct their business relationship in a manner consistent with
        HIPAA.

NOW THEREFORE, in exchange for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and
sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree to incorporate the forgoing recitals as
rewritten above and further agree as follows:

1.     Definitions. Unless otherwise defined in this Agreement, terms shall have the meanings
       established under HIPAA, including but not limited to 45 CFR §§ 160.103, 164.103,
       164.304 and 164.501.

2.      Permitted Uses and Disclosures by Business Associate. Except as otherwise limited in
        this Agreement, Business Associate may use, access, transmit, maintain, create, request or
        disclose PHI to perform functions, activities, or services for, or on behalf of, Covered

===== PAGE 68 =====
         Entity as specified by the Consulting Agreement and in a manner that does not violate
         HIPAA or other applicable law, including state privacy and security laws.

 3.      Business Associate Obligations.

         a.       Use or Disclosure of Information. Business Associate shall not use or disclose
                  PHI other than as permitted or required to perform the services described in the
                  Consulting Agreement or as required by law.

         b.       Safeguards. Business Associate shall employ administrative, physical and
                  technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality,
                  integrity, and availability of PHI, including, without limitation, appropriate training
                  and discipline of Business Associate’s work force and restrictions on access to PHI.

         c.       Agents and Subcontractors. Business Associate shall ensure that any agents and
                  subcontractors, including business associates to whom PHI is made available
                  pursuant to this Agreement agree in a binding contract to the same restrictions,
                  conditions and obligations that apply through this Agreement to Business Associate
                  with respect to such information. Business Associate further agrees to ensure that
                  any agent, subcontractor or business associate to whom it provides electronic
                  protected health information (“ePHI”) or creates, receives, maintains, or transmits
                  ePHI agrees to implement reasonable and appropriate safeguards to protect ePHI
                  and provides training. Business Associate agrees to enter into business associate
                  agreements with its business associates that meet the requirements of HIPAA and
                  the provisions of this Agreement, including but not limited to notification
                  requirements under Section 3d (entitled “Reporting”).

         d.       Reporting. Business Associate shall report to Covered Entity promptly, but no later
                  than ten (10) business days following the occurrence of any security incident,
                  privacy violations or breach as defined by HIPAA or state law, or access, use or
                  disclosure of PHI not provided for by this Agreement or the Consulting Agreement
                  of which Business Associate becomes aware (collectively a “HIPAA Incident”). At
                  the sole expense of Business Associate, Business Associate shall comply with all
                  applicable federal and state breach notification requirements and shall bear all
                  related costs associated with any HIPAA Incident, including but not limited to
                  bearing costs to provide the requisite notifications, mitigation efforts and, if
                  applicable, credit reporting protection or other consumer/patient protections as may

       THIS CONSULTING AGREEMENT (the “Agreement”) is entered into and effective as
of ______________ __, 2025 (the “Effective Date”), by and between Valley View Health &
Rehabilitation LLC, a Rhode Island limited liability company (referred to herein as “Company”),
and Lake Valley RI Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (“Consultant”).

        IN CONSIDERATION of the mutual covenants, promises and conditions contained
herein, the parties agree as follows:

Section 1.     Consulting Services.

        A.       Consultant will provide the initial, and the ongoing, consulting services as
described on Exhibit “A” hereto, and such other duties as agreed by Company and Consultant
(collectively, the “Services”), to that certain long term care facility located at 4 St Joseph St.
Woonsocket, RI 02895 (“Facility”). Consultant shall adhere to Company and Facility policies,
practices and controls, and utilize Company and Facility systems.

Section 2.     Term/Termination.

        A.      This Agreement shall commence as of the Effective Date and shall thereafter
continue for one (1) year, and shall be renewable for five (5) successive additional terms of one
(1) year each upon the parties’ mutual consent. Thereafter, this Agreement shall renew annually
for a one (1) year term until one party gives the other written notice of its intent not to renew at
least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the existing term (the “Term”).

       B.      Either party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any or
no reason, upon ninety (90) days prior written notice to the other party. Further, this Agreement
may be terminated immediately by Company upon written notice to Consultant in the event of
Consultant’s gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud in the performance of obligations under
this Agreement.

       C.     In the event of termination of this Agreement in accordance with Section 2(B) or
otherwise, Consultant shall reasonably cooperate in good faith to transition the provision of
Services to Company or its designees as expeditiously as is then reasonably practicable.
Section 3.     Compensation. In consideration of the performance of the Services, Company
shall pay Consultant a consulting fee (“Monthly Fee”) equal to five percent (5%) of the revenues
received from all sources in connection with the Facility during such period of time; provided that
the revenue shall not include or mean (i) interest or investment income of Company, (ii) capital
contributions to Company, (iii) insurance proceeds (provided however, business interruption
insurance proceeds shall be included in revenue), (iv) tax refunds, condemnation proceeds or
awards, and (v) amounts collected as trust funds or security deposits, if any, except to the extent
those security deposits are actually applied against the payments owed to the Facility.

Section 4.    Independent Contractor Status. Consultant shall not be deemed a Company
employee for the purpose of this Agreement and, on the contrary, shall be considered and treated
as an independent contractor for such purposes. Consultant specifically acknowledges and affirms

the corresponding diminution in Company’s duties and responsibilities) resulting from such status.

compensation plans including, without limitation, Workers’ Compensation and Social Security,

Section 5.     Authority. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Consultant

                                       Consulting Services

Consultant shall do the following with respect to the Facility:

   1. Resident Relations. Consult with Company in the operations of the Facility in compliance
      with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and administer a resident relations
      program which maintains visibility of consultant presence.

   2. Personnel. Advise Company with respect to employment decisions affecting on-site
      Facility employees. Except as provided herein, all on-site Facility employees shall at all
      times be Company’s employees and not employees of Consultant.

   3. Service Contracts. Recommend that Company enter into and renew contracts for
      electricity, gas, water, telephone, cable television, cleaning, fuel oil, elevator maintenance,
      vermin extermination, trash removal, linen service, pharmaceuticals and medical supplies,
      pharmacy consulting, medical director, physical and speech therapy, hospice services,
      medical equipment, and other services in the ordinary course of the operation of the
      Facility; recommend to Company the purchase of any supplies and equipment necessary
      to maintain and so operate the Facility; and ensure that Company receives any applicable
      discounts, rebates, or commissions obtained for purchases or otherwise.

   4. Maintenance and Repair. Recommend to Company any required maintenance for the
      Improvements and grounds of the Facility including, without limitation, interior and
      exterior cleaning, painting and decorating, plumbing, carpentry, and other normal
      maintenance and repair work.

   5. Collection. Recommend to Company best practices to request, demand, collect, receive,
      and receipt all charges due from residents and otherwise due Company with respect to the
      Facility. Consultant may recommend that certain uncollectible accounts be charged off to
      a bad debt expense after reasonable efforts have been exhausted for collections, subject to
      Company’s final approval.

   6. Expenses. Assist Company, as directed by Company, with the contest and/or payment of
      all Facility expenses on or before that date after which interest or penalty will begin to
      accrue thereon.

   7. Reports. As soon as reasonable and practicable each calendar month, render to Company a
      statement of income and expenses showing the results of operation of the Facility for the
      preceding month and of the fiscal year to date. As soon as reasonably practical, but in no
      event later than twenty (20) days following the close of each quarter, render to Company a
      statement of income and expenses showing the results of operation of the Facility for the
      preceding quarter and of the fiscal year to date. As soon as reasonable and practicable
      after the end of each fiscal year, Consultant shall deliver to Company profit and loss
      statements, prepared on an accrual basis in accordance with generally accepted accounting
      principles consistently applied. All such monthly reports shall be in the format normally
      utilized by Consultant. Company may, regularly and/or from time to time, require that the

===== PAGE 83 =====
         annual financial statements of the Facility be audited, reviewed or compiled by a reputable
         accounting firm. Additionally, Consultant shall provide Company with all such financial
         and other reports and/or documents as required by any lenders of Company to enable
         Company to comply with the reporting requirements set forth in the applicable loan
         documents.

    8. Records. Recommend and assist Company in implementing best practices for maintaining
       a system of office records, books, and accounts, and any additional information or records
       reasonably required by Company for the preparation of federal, state, and local tax returns,
       all in a manner reasonably satisfactory to Company. Company and others designated by
       Company, including Company’s auditors and accountants, shall have, upon reasonable
       notice to Consultant, during normal business hours, access to and the right to audit and
       make copies of such records, accounts, and books, and all vouchers, files and all other
       material pertaining to the Facility and this Agreement that may be maintained at the address
       of Consultant.

    9. Legal Proceedings. Consultant shall make recommendations to Company related to the
       institution and prosecution of such actions and proceedings necessary to effect the
       purposes, perform the services, and take the actions contemplated by this Agreement.

    10. Process Insurance Claims. If requested by Company, Consultant shall assist Company in
        the processing of all claims under any insurance coverages pertaining to the Facility in a
        reasonably expeditious manner, so as to minimize delay in receipt by the Facility of the
        proceeds of such insurance.

        rates at other comparable facilities in the market area.

                               BUSINESS ASSOCIATE ADDENDUM

This Business Associate Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of the Effective
Date of the CONSULTING AGREEMENT (“Consulting Agreement”) to which this Agreement
is attached by and between Company (“Covered Entity”) and Consultant (“Business Associate”),
and is attached to and made part of the Consulting Agreement. Covered Entity and Business
Associate are sometimes referred to individually as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.”
Capitalized terms not defined in this Agreement shall have the meanings set forth in the Consulting
Agreement.

                                          RECITALS

     A. The Parties acknowledge that they are required to comply with the Health Insurance
        Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and its accompanying regulations as amended
        from time to time, including the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Heath
        Information (“Privacy Rule”) and the Security Standards for the Protection of Electronic
        Protected Health Information (the “Security Rule”), as well as Subtitle D of the Health
        Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act of 2009 (“HITECH”) of
        the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act and its accompanying regulations, as
        amended from time to time (collectively, “HIPAA”).

     B. Covered Entity is a “covered entity,” as defined in HIPAA.

     C. Business Associate is a “business associate” as defined by HIPAA.

D.      Business Associate provides consulting services to Covered Entity (collectively, the
        “Services”) in accordance with the Consulting Agreement to which this Agreement is
        attached. In accordance with the terms of the Consulting Agreement, Business Associate
        may use, disclose, create, receive, maintain, or transmit, as applicable, on behalf of
        Covered Entity, protected health information (“PHI”) for purposes of providing the
        Services.
E.      The Parties desire to conduct their business relationship in a manner consistent with
        HIPAA.

NOW THEREFORE, in exchange for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and
sufficiency of which are acknowledged, the Parties agree to incorporate the forgoing recitals as
rewritten above and further agree as follows:

1.     Definitions. Unless otherwise defined in this Agreement, terms shall have the meanings
       established under HIPAA, including but not limited to 45 CFR §§ 160.103, 164.103,
       164.304 and 164.501.

        disclose PHI to perform functions, activities, or services for, or on behalf of, Covered

thirty (30) days after delivery of a bill therefor together with reasonable back-up documentation.

       10.2    Casualty and Condemnation.
         10.2.1 If, prior to Closing, proceedings for the condemnation of the Property, or any
interest therein, or any portion thereof, are commenced by any governmental authority having
jurisdiction to do so, or the Improvements are damaged or destroyed by fire or other major casualty,
Purchaser may, at its option, terminate this Agreement by written notice to Seller given within
fifteen (15) days after Seller advises Purchaser in writing of (i) the occurrence of a condemnation
proceeding and (ii) in the event of a casualty, if elected by Seller, that it does not intend to restore
the Property prior to Closing. If Purchaser terminates this Agreement, the Good-Faith Deposit shall
be returned to Purchaser and neither party shall have any further rights, obligations or liability
under this Agreement, except those that expressly survive termination. Seller and Purchaser shall
cooperate regarding the recovery of available insurance coverage with respect thereto and the
probable amount of any condemnation award or insurance proceeds recoverable on account
thereof. In the event, however, that the cost of repairing the Property is equal to or less than
$250,000.00 (as reasonably determined by the Parties or their agents), the Parties shall
consummate the purchase and sale of the Property without reduction of the Purchase Price and
Seller shall, on the Closing Date, pay or assign to Purchaser all insurance proceeds in connection
with such damage or destruction actually received or receivable by Seller, less, Seller if applicable,
any amounts expended to repair or restore the buildings, improvements and fixtures at the
Property. In no event shall Seller be obligated to perform any repair or restoration of the buildings,
improvements and fixtures at the Property; provided that Purchaser shall not the right to terminate
this Agreement pursuant to the provisions of this Section 10.2 unless the cost of repairing the
Property is determined to exceed $250,000 and the actions or inaction of Allaire or its agents on
site at the Property were not the primary cause of the damage to the Property.

         AGREEMENT FOR PURCHASE AND SALE – TRINITY FACILITY
        This Agreement for Purchase and Sale (the “Agreement”) is made as of the 7th day of
April, 2025 (the “Execution Date”), by and between SUMMIT WOONSOCKET, LLC
(“Seller”), a Delaware limited liability company, having an address at c/o Summit Healthcare
REIT, 23382 Mill Creek Drive, Suite 125, Laguna Hills, California 92653, and the owner of the
real property and improvements located at 4 Saint Joseph Street, Woonsocket, Rhode Island,
currently leased to ASLC OPCO RI I, LLC (“ASLC I”), a Rhode Island limited liability company,
pursuant to a Lease dated May 20, 2014, as amended (the “Trinity Lease”) for operation by ASLC
I of the Trinity Health and Rehabilitation Center, a 185 bed skilled nursing facility (“Trinity
Facility”); and VALLEY VIEW HEALTH AND REHABILITATION PROPCO LLC
(“Purchaser”), an entity formed and controlled by Allaire Health Care, Inc. (“Allaire”), the
current operator of Trinity Facility pursuant to a management agreement dated July 18, 2023
(“Management Agreement”). Purchaser and Seller are sometimes collectively referred to herein
as “Parties” and individually, as a “Party.”
       WHEREAS, Jeremy B. Savage, Esq., solely in his capacity as permanent receiver of
ASLC RI I and the Trinity Facility (“Receiver”) appointed pursuant to an order of the Providence
Superior Court (the “Court”) dated June 21, 2023 (the proceeding, the “Receivership Action”),
has negotiated terms for sale of substantially all of the personal property assets owned by ASLC I
and used in connection with operation of the Trinity Facility to a Purchaser Affiliate(s) (“Trinity
Personalty”), and for transition of the operation of the Trinity Facility to Allaire or its designee,
pending approval of the Rhode Island Department of Health (“RIDOH”) and other regulatory
approvals;
        WHEREAS, in addition, a Seller Affiliate and a Purchaser Affiliate have negotiated terms
through a contemporaneously executed purchase agreement relating to the sale of the real property
and improvements leased to ASLC RI II, LLC (“ASLC II”) d/b/a Hebert Health Care (“Hebert
Facility”)(the sale relating to the “Hebert Property”) to the Purchaser Affiliate; with the Receiver
having also negotiated terms for sale of substantially all of the personal property assets (“Hebert
Personalty”) owned by ASLC II (collectively, with ASLC I, the “Companies”) that are used in
connection with operation of the Hebert Facility to a Purchaser Affiliate(s) pursuant to a receiver’s
bill of sale (the purchase of the Trinity Personalty and the Hebert Personalty, the “Asset
Purchase”);
       WHEREAS, in connection with the closing of the sale of the Trinity Personalty to
Purchaser, Seller desires to sell and Purchaser desires to purchase the real property upon which the
Trinity Facility is operated (defined below as the “Trinity Property”), upon the terms and
conditions hereinafter set forth; and
       WHEREAS, in connection with the purchase of the Trinity Property and the Hebert
Property (“Real Property Sales”), Purchaser has agreed to fund a deposit of Six Hundred One
Thousand Seven Hundred Twenty-Four and 25/100 Dollars USD ($601,724.25) to be held in
escrow by the Title Insurer pending closing of the Real Property Sales (“Sale Transactions”), of
which Three Hundred Thousand Eight Hundred Sixty-Two and 25/100 Dollars USD
($300,862.25) (“Good-Faith Deposit”) shall be allocated to the sale of the Trinity Property and
applied pursuant to the provisions below.

      NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the Property and the mutual covenants and
agreements hereinafter set forth, the Parties hereto hereby agree as follows:
       1.       The Property. Purchaser agrees to purchase and Seller agrees to sell, pursuant to the
terms set forth in this Agreement, the following described property (collectively, the “Property”):
       1.1     that certain parcel of land described on Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated
by reference located within the City of Woonsocket, Rhode Island, designated by the City of
Woonsocket Assessor as Assessor’s Plat 23, Lot 60, and located at 4 Saint Joseph Street,
Woonsocket, Rhode Island 02895 and commonly known as “Trinity Health and Rehabilitation
Center” (the “Land”);
       1.2    All existing buildings, structures, and other improvements located on the Property,
including without limitation, the walkways, the road improvements, parking facilities, and all other
improvements of whatever kind and nature which have previously been made, installed or erected
and are now located on any part of the Property (collectively, the “Improvements”);
        1.3     All appurtenances, hereditaments, easements, reversionary rights, and all other
rights, privileges, and entitlements belonging to or running with the Property, including but not
limited to all of Seller’s right, title and interest in and to any and all land laying in the bed of any
street, road, cul-de-sac, alley or access way, open or closed, existing, vacated or proposed,
adjoining, adjacent to or contiguous to the land, and all zoning and land use entitlements and
development rights pertaining to the Property;
        1.4    all tangible and intangible personal property owned by Seller and located on or used
in conjunction with the Property, if any (collectively, the “Personal Property”);
       1.5    All applicable licenses, permits, variances, authorizations and approvals pertaining
to ownership of the Property that are held exclusively by Seller, to the extent assignable, if any
(the “Licenses”); and
        1.6     those certain contract rights pertaining to the ownership or operation of the Property
which are assignable (and Purchaser agrees to assume) and would affect the Property after Closing
(as herein defined) as set forth on Schedule 1.6 attached hereto, if any, but excluding rights to the
return of any prepayments or deposits and excluding the Trinity Lease, which will be deemed
terminated following the occurrence of the Closing (the “Contracts”).
        2.        Purchase Price. The purchase price for the Property (“Purchase Price”) is
Twelve Million Seventy-Five Thousand Five Hundred Ninety-Four and 58/100 Dollars
($12,075,594.58). The Purchase Price, subject to the credits, prorations, and adjustments set forth
in this Agreement, and less the Good-Faith Deposit previously funded towards the Purchase Price
held by Title Insurer, shall be paid:
               (i) by Purchaser to Seller by wire transfer to Title Insurer's account, if Closing
occurs in escrow, or to counsel to Seller, at the time of Closing, and

               (ii) by the Purchaser or Title Insurer, as applicable, to Seller by wire transfer to
Seller's account immediately upon Closing.

        Wired funds must be received in the Title Insurer’s account prior to 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time
on the Closing Date. Purchaser shall undertake to timely facilitate the retention of the Title Insurer
for all Closing related tasks contemplated by this Agreement.

       3.      Review of the Property; Closing Conditions.
        3.1     The Purchaser acknowledges that the Receiver is in possession of the Property
pursuant to the Trinity Lease, with Allaire operating the Trinity Facility on a day to day basis, such
that Purchaser has had sufficient access the Property to inspect the structural portions of the
Property prior to execution of this Agreement, and that prior to Closing, Purchaser will remain in
exclusive possession of the Property. While Purchaser may desire to conduct further physical and
environmental studies (including a Phase I environmental assessment) (“Further Studies”) as
expressly required for Purchaser to close its loan with Customers (defined below), the results of
those studies will not impact Purchaser’s obligations to move forward unless otherwise expressly
set forth herein. In undertaking Further Studies, Purchaser, agrees (a) that no invasive testing may
be conducted without Seller's prior consent, which may be withheld by Seller in its sole discretion,
and (b) not to cause any damage or make any physical changes to the Property, and (c) not to
unreasonably interfere with the operation of the Trinity Facility and care of the patients receiving
care at the Trinity Facility. Seller and/or its representative shall have the right to be present to
observe any testing or other inspection performed on the Property (and Purchaser shall provide
Seller with reasonable advance notice of all testing and inspections to be performed on the
Property). Purchaser shall indemnify, defend and hold Seller harmless from and against any
claims, damages, expenses or losses, resulting from harm that is judicially determined to be
attributable to Purchaser’s activities in respect of the Further Studies relating to the Property, with
such obligation to survive termination and Closing.
        3.2    Upon written request from Purchaser (which can be by e-mail), only to the extent
not provided by Seller prior to the Execution Date, Seller will deliver to Purchaser copies of all of
the following for Purchaser’s records, to the extent not previously provided by Seller:
       (a)     a copy of the most recent environmental report relating to the Property (if any);
       (b)     copies of the most recent survey of the Property (if any);
       (c)     copies of the most recent notice of change in assessed value or tax rate for the
               Property;
       (d)     a copy of the existing title policy for the Property, Owners Policy of Title Insurance
               issued by Commonwealth Land Title Insurance Company, Policy Number
               6122739B (“Existing Policy”); and
       (e)     a list of all litigation relating to the Property pending against Seller or the Property,
               if any, to which the Seller is a party, other than the ASLC I receivership action.
       3.3     Purchaser acknowledges that it does not require any additional time to complete
any Further Studies or diligence except relating to the title and survey, which are governed by
Section 4. Purchaser shall have no ability to terminate this Agreement or to extend the Closing
Date after the Execution Date, except as set forth in Sections 3.5, 4.1, 4.2, 10.2.1, 10.10.2, or
10.10.3 below.

        3.4     Purchaser agrees that any information obtained by Purchaser or its authorized
agents in the conduct of its due diligence will be treated as confidential pursuant to Section 10.12.

      3.5    Global Closing Conditions. Seller agrees that Purchaser’s obligation to
consummate the Sales Transactions is strictly contingent and conditioned upon (i) prior to the

Closing Date and in order to accomplish a timely Closing, Purchaser obtaining any necessary

Property as a skilled nursing home facility in the substantially same manner as the Property is

Date despite Purchaser’s commercially reasonable efforts, Purchaser, in its sole discretion, has the
right to either (a) terminate this Agreement by providing written notice to Seller made no later than
5:00 p.m. EST on the Closing Date, in which case the Good-Faith Deposit shall be returned to
Purchaser and neither Party shall have any other rights or obligations hereunder except those that
expressly survive termination of this Agreement or (b) extend the Closing Date by a period not to
exceed thirty (30) days (the “Extended Closing Date”) by providing written notice to Seller made
no later than 5:00 p.m. EST on the Closing Date, provided that Purchaser shall be obligated to pay
in the first instance, or reimburse Seller for, the cost of satisfying any additional sewer, water, and
real estate taxes assessed with regard to the Property pending the occurrence of the Extended
Closing Date, which obligation shall expressly survive termination of this Agreement. If Purchaser
has not obtained and/or consummated the RIDOH Approval, Customers Loan, and Asset Purchase
on or prior to the Extended Closing Date despite its commercially reasonable best efforts to do so,
then, unless Purchaser, in its sole discretion, elects to waive any such unsatisfied condition, either
Seller or Purchaser may, in each of its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement with written notice
to the other Party made no later than 5:00 p.m. EST on the Extended Closing Date. If this
Agreement is terminated as permitted by this Section 3.5 other than as the result of breach by
Purchaser of its obligations hereunder, the Good-Faith Deposit shall be returned to Purchaser and
neither Party shall have any other rights or obligations hereunder except those that expressly
survive termination of this Agreement. As part of its commercially reasonable efforts, as promptly
as practicable after execution and delivery of this Agreement and no later than ten (10) Business
Days after the Effective Date of this Agreement, Purchaser, at its sole cost and expense, shall (and
shall cause its affiliates to) make all required filings and promptly pursue all material approvals,
permits and orders with respect to the Real Property Sales and Asset Purchase, including, but not
limited to, the RIDOH, to endeavor to ensure that the RIDOH Approval and commitment for the
Customers Loan are obtained on a timely basis. Purchaser agrees to provide Seller with copies of
all filings with the RIDOH, as permitted by the RIDOH, and to otherwise keep Seller apprised of
the status of Purchaser’s effort to timely obtain the RIDOH Approval.

        3.6     The Parties agree that the effective date of this Agreement shall not occur until the

the Title Insurer within three (3) business days of the Execution Date or this Agreement shall be
of no further force and effect, unless otherwise agreed to by Seller.

        4.      Title.

        4.1      On or prior to the Effective Date, Purchaser agrees to order at its expense (and upon
receipt, to promptly deliver copies to Seller): (i) an updated commitment for a ALTA Owner’s title
insurance policy with respect to the Property from Landmark Abstract Agency, LLC (the “Title
Insurer”) in the amount of the Purchase Price (the “Title Commitment”); and (ii) copies of all
documents relating to title exceptions referred to therein. Upon its execution of the Agreement,
Purchaser may also order, at Purchaser’s sole expense, a current survey of the Property made in
accordance with Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/ACSM Land Title Surveys
(2016) pursuant to the accuracy standards of an Urban Survey (the “Survey”). Within thirty (30)
days of the Effective Date, Purchaser shall notify Seller of any objection Purchaser may have to
any exceptions reported in the Title Commitment or the Survey (other than with regard to those
that are Acceptable Exceptions, defined below) (the “Unacceptable Exceptions”). Seller will have
five (5) days after receipt of Purchaser’s notice within which to notify Purchaser whether Seller
either (i) elects to cure the Unacceptable Exceptions, or (ii) elects not to cure the Unacceptable
Exceptions (“Seller’s Response Notice”). If Seller agrees to cure the Unacceptable Exceptions,
Seller will be obligated to do so at its cost on or prior to Closing. If Seller elects item (ii) above
or fails to deliver a timely Seller’s Response Notice, Purchaser shall have the option to (x)
terminate this Agreement by delivering written notice thereof to Seller within five (5) days of the
post-marked date of Seller’s Response Notice (or, in the event that Seller fails to deliver Seller’s
Response Notice, within five (5) days after the date on which Seller’s Response Notice was due)
(“Title Termination Notice”), in which case the Good-Faith Deposit shall be returned to
Purchaser and neither Party shall have any other rights or obligations hereunder except those that
expressly survive termination of this Agreement, or (y) waive any defect of title existing as of the
Effective Date, accept such title as Seller can convey and proceed to Closing (subject to
Purchaser’s other right of termination under Section 3.5). Purchaser’s failure to deliver Title
Termination Notice within said five (5) day period shall be deemed Purchaser’s election of option
(y) above. In the event that Purchaser does not deliver to Seller written notice of the Unacceptable
Exceptions on or prior to the expiration of the Review Period, Purchaser shall be deemed to have
waived its right to object to any matters of title existing as of the Effective Date. If Purchaser
terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 4.1, the Good-Faith Deposit shall be returned
to Purchaser and neither party will have any further rights or obligations hereunder unless
expressly set forth herein.

         4.2    If any other recorded exception to title is discovered after the Title Commitment is
delivered to Purchaser and prior to Closing that is (i) not the result of action of Allaire or Purchaser;
or (ii) is not an Acceptable Exception, and Purchaser does not elect to waive such additional
exception upon the first to occur of (a) the Closing or (b) seven (7) days after being notified of
such exception and to proceed with the consummation of the Closing, Seller will have fifteen (15)
days after the expiration of said seven (7) day period (and Closing will be delayed if necessary, so
that it occurs not earlier than twenty-two (22) days after Purchaser is notified of such exception)
after having received notice of such exception in which to use commercially reasonable efforts to
eliminate or to induce the Title Insurer to insure over (subject to Purchaser’s approval, not to be
unreasonably withheld) such exception, and if such exception is not eliminated or insured over as
aforesaid within said fifteen (15) day period, Purchaser may terminate this Agreement, in which
case the Good-Faith Deposit shall be returned to Purchaser and neither Party shall have any other
rights or obligations hereunder except those that expressly survive termination of this Agreement,

                                                   5

or instead, proceed to close the sale subject to such exception. In using commercially reasonable
efforts to eliminate or to induce the Title Insurer to insure over Unacceptable Exceptions, Seller
will not be required to litigate or to expend more than $25,000 in the aggregate.

       4.3    Without limiting the foregoing, the following shall be deemed “Acceptable
Exceptions” and not “Unacceptable Exceptions”:

       (a)    Real property taxes and assessments that have accrued or otherwise become due
and payable for tax periods from and after July 18, 2023 and prior to the Closing;
       (b)     The standard printed exceptions contained in owner's title insurance policies;
       (c)     Zoning and other regulatory laws and ordinances affecting the Property;
       (d)     Conditions, easements and restrictions of record;
        (g)    The Trinity Lease and any and all documents related thereto, subject to the
obligation of Seller to deliver the termination of the Trinity Lease as provided herein;
       (h)      Any lien or attachment held by a third-party vendor, materialmen, contractor, or
supplier to the Trinity Facility retained by or under contract with Allaire;
       (i)      Any other matters that do not materially impact the ability of Purchaser to continue
to operate the Trinity Facility from the Property or result in a monetary lien in an amount equal to
or more than seventy-five thousand and 00/100 dollars ($75,000.00);
       (j)     Any other matter that is the result of any action taken by Allaire or Purchaser; and
       (k)    Any matters that are approved in writing by Purchaser or deemed approved by
Purchaser in accordance with this Agreement or that are caused or otherwise permitted by
Purchaser.
       4.4      At Closing, Seller shall convey to Purchaser good and marketable title to the
Property, free and clear of any and all liens, security interests and all other defects of title
whatsoever with the exception of the Acceptable Exceptions. Notwithstanding anything to the
contrary in this Agreement, Seller shall be obligated, on or before the Closing Date to discharge
and remove of record at its expense any and all lien, encumbrance, mortgage or deed of trust
securing the payment of money other than a lien or encumbrance relating to an Acceptable
Exception (“Seller Monetary Liens”). To enable Seller to make conveyance as herein provided,
Seller may, on the Closing Date, use the purchase money or any portion thereof to clear the title
of any or all Seller Monetary Liens provided that all instruments so procured are recorded
simultaneously with the delivery of the Deed or that provision for prompt recording thereof
reasonably satisfactory to Purchaser’s attorneys are made on the Closing Date. Seller shall have
no obligation or undertaking with regard to any liens, claims or encumbrances other than Seller
Monetary Liens, unless Seller elects to cure Unacceptable Exceptions pursuant to Section 4.1
above.
       4.5   Survey. Purchaser acknowledges and agrees that, prior to the execution of this

5.1.1 to the knowledge of Seller, Seller has neither received written notice of, nor been informed

planned to be instituted, with respect to the Property or any part thereof.
        5.1.2          Status of Seller and Closing Documents. This Agreement has been, and all

        5.1.3           Non-Foreign Status. Seller is not a foreign person within the meaning of

        5.1.5        No Default. The execution and delivery of this Agreement, and

U.S.C. § 1251 et seq.), Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (42 U.S.C. § 6901 et seq.), Safe
Drinking Water Act (42 U.S.C. § 3000 (f) et seq.), Toxic Substances Control Act (15 U.S.C. § 2601
et seq.), Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. § 7401 et seq.), Comprehensive Environmental Response,
Compensation and Liability Act (42 U.S.C. § 9601 et seq.), and other similar statutes or ordinances
of the State of Rhode Island. The term “Environment” means the ambient air, surface water, ground
water, and/or soil.

         10.2.1 If, prior to Closing, proceedings for the condemnation of the Property, or any

thereof. In the event, however, that the cost of repairing the Property is equal to or less than

A certain parcel of land together with all buildings and improvements thereon, situated on the
easterly side of Maple Street in the City of Woonsocket, County of Providence and State of
Rhode Island, bounded and described as follows:

northerly bounding westerly by the easterly line of Maple Street, three hundred forty (340.00)
feet to a corner; thence turning an interior angle of ninety (90º) degrees and running easterly
bounding northerly by land now or formerly of Jean Baptist, Jr. and Irene F. Ethier, a distance of
one hundred fifty (150.00) feet to a corner; thence turning an interior angle of two hundred
seventy (270º) degrees and running northerly bounding westerly by land now or formerly of Jean
Baptiste, Jr. and Irene F. Ethier, a distance of fifty (50.00) feet to a corner; thence turning an
interior angle of ninety (90º) and running easterly bounding northerly by land now or formerly of
Richard A. and Jeanne L. Houle a distance of one hundred fifty (150.00) feet to a corner; thence
